builds.name: Ashnard: Mad King
builds.c: Uplift Imbue A/S / S/D Hold Guide

builds.name: Madness in the Mirror
builds.desc:
A purely enemy phase build, this takes advantage of Ashnard's impressive defensive stats to tank opponents and subsequently crush them with his excellent offensive capabilities.
【 Weapon 】
Gurgurant is his unique weapon, and the only real choice for him. Not only does it have the very helpful effect of a slightly upgraded Atk/Def Rein before that skill has even been released, but it also has a built-in Iote's Shield, meaning that Ashnard — who has the stats to be a defensive tank — doesn't need to waste a slot on Iote's to negate his defences being bypassed by bows or specialized tomes.
【 Assist 】
Reposition is an old standby, and works very well to help snatch allies out of danger.
Swap is a good alternative if that fits your play style better.
【 Special 】
Bonfire hits hard, scaling off Ashnard's high Def stat, and is the best choice if he's only engaging in a couple of battles (or extended battles against opponents who can't appreciably dent his defences).
Noontime or Sol are a good options if you're worried about keeping up with Quick Riposte 3's requirement through longer engagements; although they won't boost Ashnard's immediate damage output, they will keep him healthy enough to continually manage follow ups, which on the grand scale is generally more damaging to opponents.
【 A Skill 】
Distant Counter is the best option for Ashnard. This build is purely enemy phase, so he wants to make sure he can consistently retaliate on enemy phase regardless of his opponent's range.
Distant Foil is a choice that increases both his Atk and Def upon being assaulted by physical damage dealers regardless of range, but Ashnard has a high enough Res stat (especially with Mirror Stance 2 as a Seal) that he'd prefer to be able to retaliate against mages as well.
【 B Skill 】
Quick Riposte 3 is a boring but highly effective skill for his B slot, affording him a guaranteed follow up attack so long as his health meets the threshold for activation. Considering his low Spd, he'll almost always need the skill to make follow ups at all.
Guard 3 shuts down enemy Specials that could otherwise make a dent in his defences, but has a 10% higher threshold for activation than Quick Riposte and is best used with a healing Special.
【 C Skill 】
Flexible as always, C skills are up to preference; Smoke skills are good general choices to benefit both Ashnard and his team, and Wave skills give visible stat boosts to him and any adjacent allies every other turn.
Goad Fliers is equal to Hone Fliers, Fortify Fliers, or Ward Fliers if Ashnard is placed on a Flying team — it just depends on what the team needs.
【 Sacred Seal w/ Quick Riposte as B Skill 】
Mirror Stance 2 boosts both his Atk and Res on enemy phase, allowing him to deal more damage as well as making his Res equal his Def, allowing him to tank magic just as effectively as physical hits.
Atk/Def Solo 3 is a fantastic choice if you're more concerned with Def than Res and want dual-phase power, but it depends on team composition; it likely won't work out as well if he's on a Flier team and is getting buffed by adjacent allies' Hone and Fortify skills.
Sturdy Stance 2 is an alternative to Atk/Def Solo; its combat boost is lower by 2 points, and it's enemy phase only, but it doesn't matter how Ashnard is positioned.
Fierce Stance 3 is an option if you're looking to maximize his damage output instead of worrying about his defences, although you will be giving up Def/Res+4 in exchange for 2 more points of Atk; whether that's a fair trade is up to you.
Steady Stance 3 / Warding Stance 3, conversely, are available if you'd prefer to sacrifice Atk+4 for an additional Def/Res+2.
【 Sacred Seal w/ Guard as B Skill 】
Quick Riposte 3 is recommended over Stance Seals if you're using Guard 3 as Ashnard's B skill instead; the ability to strike twice overshadows the Atk+4/6 the Atk-boosting Stances give him. In the case of a Guard/Quick Riposte combo, a healing Special is highly recommended in order to keep Ashnard above both thresholds so that the two skills don't become useless dead weight once his health drops.
